_comment: Mountain ranges and rivers (core/world/worldgen/stage_barriers.gd). Sizes are tiles unless they say otherwise. A world narrower than min_world has neither. range: one crest per mountain stretch with biomes on both sides (one more per range_every tiles of it); crest_share = its width as a fraction of the world's, clamped to crest; walls = how many cliffed walls stand on it, wall_w = each wall's share of its slot, height = wall height over half-width, terrace = rows between ledges: at least 10, since a body reaches 7.75 rows (6.75 of jump, 1 of step) and a neighbouring column can take one off. margin = columns either side kept clear of towns. pass_h = clear rows on the pass; open_cut = rock this thin over it is cut away to the sky, thicker is a gallery. torch_every = columns between lights in a gallery. under: cover = rows of rock over the under-route at its shallowest, search = how far outward from the margin a mouth is looked for, shelf = columns of level ground either side of a mouth, wander = rows it wanders. river: count = one per so many tiles of world width, biomes = where they run, with ford_p the chance of a ford. width = [lo, hi] of a channel (its sides slope a row a column), banks = columns of level ground each side, deep = rows of water under a bridge, drop = rows from the bank to the water (bridge), ford_drop = rows from the bank to the ford's bed (a ford has one row of water), seal = rows of river bed laid under it, flat_gap = columns kept from a town's flat. cost: a route's length grows by this fraction of the world's width per crossing.
